primary_reads.author: Seiichi Kamada
primary_reads.title: Braid presentation of virtual knots and welded knots
primary_reads.read_scope: Sections 2 and 3, Proposition 3.1, Theorem 3.2, exact right/left exchange formulas, virtual versus welded presentation, and statements on exchange independence; braiding proof input noted rather than fully recertified.
primary_reads.outcome: Exact input matches the candidate: defining relations, conjugation, all three right stabilizations, both exchanges, every oriented virtual link represented. Does not itself state an even-only presentation.

primary_reads.authors: Louis H. Kauffman and Sofia Lambropoulou
primary_reads.title: Virtual Braids and the L-Move
primary_reads.read_scope: Algebraic Markov theorem in section 4, left inclusion in Remark 6, and section 5 exact comparison with both Kamada exchanges and equivalent move lists.
primary_reads.outcome: Independent primary corroboration of the imported calculus. A different local move list does not imply that the target secretly requires such locality or already supplies this even-only formulation.

primary_reads.authors: Roger Fenn, Denis P. Ilyutko, Louis H. Kauffman, Vassily O. Manturov
primary_reads.title: Unsolved Problems in Virtual Knot Theory and Combinatorial Knot Theory
primary_reads.read_scope: Item 42 and neighboring items in both author and publisher text; printed page 34 in author version, printed page 37 in publication.
primary_reads.outcome: Target explicitly asks that only even-strand braids occur in the reformulation. No bounded support, minimality, plat, framed, or stronger homological preservation condition is attached to item 42. This 2014 source does not certify current openness in 2026.

primary_reads.title: A Markov theorem for generalized plat decomposition
primary_reads.read_scope: Abstract, introduction, and definition of generalized plat pairing.
primary_reads.outcome: Even strand counts arise from top and bottom plat pairing. That closure convention differs from the candidate's arbitrary ordinary closures; no identical ordinary virtual even-only theorem verified here.

primary_reads.author: Ivan Smith
primary_reads.title: Monodromy, Vanishing Cycles, Knots and the Adjoint Quotient
primary_reads.read_scope: Specific article sections 2.3–2.4, printed page 286; not the entire collected volume.
primary_reads.outcome: Doubles beta in Br_n to beta times identity in Br_2n with auxiliary horseshoe data; original n still participates in Markov comparisons. No identical arbitrary ordinary even-only formulation verified.
